mainTopic: רבי's unique greatness, and the rules for deals made by a deaf-mute and by young children
overview: רב reports that when רבי's court voted, they asked him first. The גמרא asks why, since a משנה says that outside capital cases the vote starts with the greatest judge. It answers that רבי's court always started with the junior judges. The same teacher praises רבי: from משה until רבי, no one person was supreme in both Torah and worldly greatness. The גמרא tests this against יהושע, שאול, דוד, שלמה, חזקיה and עזרא. Each time it answers either that someone else was their equal, or that the claim means being unmatched for all one's years. רב אחא בריה דרבא says the same about the period from רבי to רב אשי. A new משנה then rules that a deaf-mute can buy and sell movable items by gestures (בן בתירא: even by lip movements), and that young children's deals in movable items count. The גמרא discusses whether this reaches גיטין, at what age children qualify, why the rule exists, how big a price mistake is allowed, and whether a child's gift counts. Between these it explains the words מלתחה and מלמלא. The amud ends with a new משנה about rules made מפני דרכי שלום, such as the order of the Torah reading.

steps.title: רב was asked first in רבי's vote
steps.stepSummary: רב reports that he was present when רבי's court voted, and they started the vote with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: I was there when רבי's court counted the votes, and they started counting with me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב tells us he took part in the vote in רבי's court, and they asked for his opinion first. This report sets up the question the גמרא will ask next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was a young, junior member of the court, yet his vote came first. That detail matters, because there is a set order for who speaks first in a בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: The counting of votes in a court
The court or study hall of רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: I was present at the counting of the vote in the house of Rabbi,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב. "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and they began counting with me myself first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the vote in רבי's court about the new rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי's court, the voting began with רב, a junior member.

steps.title: A משנה says voting starts with the greatest judge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's report from a משנה: in non-capital cases, voting starts with the greatest judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: in money cases and purity cases, they start with the greatest judge. Only in capital cases do they start from the side, with the junior judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב could have voted first. A משנה says that only in capital cases do they start with the junior judges, and this was not a capital case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives two orders. In ממונות and טהרות they start with the greatest judge, out of respect. In נפשות they start from the side, so the junior judges are not swayed by the senior ones. רבי's vote was not about a capital case, so the greatest judge, רבי himself, should have gone first, not רב.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn? (opens a challenge from a משנה)
Capital cases, where a life is at stake
From the side: the junior judges on the side benches

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
In monetary cases, and cases of ritual purity and impurity,
they begin with the greatest judge,
but in capital cases they begin from the side!
phrases.notes: "From the side" means the youngest judges, who sat on the side benches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's report in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the vote in רבי's court started with him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case was not a capital case, so by the משנה the vote should have begun with the greatest judge, not with a junior one.

steps.title: רבי's court always started from the junior judges
steps.stepSummary: רבה בריה דרבא (or רבי הלל בריה דרבי וולס) answers that רבי's court was different: every vote there began from the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה son of רבא said, and some say it was רבי הלל son of רבי וולס: the voting in רבי's court was different. All their votes began from the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In רבי's court, every vote started with the junior judges, not just votes in capital cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule is the normal order, but רבי's court was an exception. It used the "from the side" order for every kind of case. It is commonly explained that once רבי spoke, no one would dare to disagree, so they let the junior judges speak first.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a second opinion on who said it)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's order (greatest first in non-capital cases) is the normal rule. רבי's court was an exception that always began with the junior judges.

phrases.english: Rabba, son of Rava, said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי הִילֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי וָולָס:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Hillel, son of Rabbi Volas:
The counting in the house of Rabbi is different,
because all of their countings
they would begin from the side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: רבי's court had its own practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every court follows the משנה's order, so רב could not have voted first in a non-capital case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's court always began from the junior judges, so it makes sense that רב voted first.

steps.title: Torah and greatness together, from משה until רבי
steps.stepSummary: The same teacher praises רבי: from משה until רבי, Torah and worldly greatness were never found together in one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same teacher said: from the days of משה until רבי, we never found Torah and greatness together in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא was just talking about רבי's court, it adds another teaching from the same teacher in praise of רבי. This is a new statement, not part of the question and answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "In one place" means in one person. רבי was both the greatest Torah scholar and a man of great worldly standing, such as wealth and power. The statement says no one between משה and רבי had both at that level.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah greatness and worldly greatness (wealth, power)
In one place, meaning in a single person

steps.whatToRemember: רבי was unusual: he had top Torah greatness and top worldly greatness together, something not seen from משה until his time.

phrases.english: And Rabba, son of Rava, said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי הִילֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי ווֹלֶס:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Hillel, son of Rabbi Volas:
From the days of Moses until Rabbi

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָצִינוּ תּוֹרָה וּגְדוּלָּה בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: we did not find Torah and greatness in one place.
phrases.notes: "Greatness" here means worldly standing, like wealth and power.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִימוֹת מֹשֶׁה וְעַד רַבִּי לֹא מָצִינוּ תּוֹרָה וּגְדוּלָּה בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching from the same teacher about רבי's greatness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From משה until רבי, no single person combined supreme Torah greatness with supreme worldly greatness.

steps.title: Wasn't יהושע such a person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim from step 4 by pointing to יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was there really no such person? Wasn't there יהושע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the praise of רבי. It names יהושע as a leader who seems to have had both תורה and greatness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 claimed that no one between משה and רבי combined תורה and worldly greatness. יהושע led the whole nation and was משה's top student, so he looks like a counterexample.

keyTerms.meaning: And was there not? (a surprised challenge)
משה's successor as leader of the nation

steps.confusionAlert: This begins a long chain. Every challenge has the same goal: to find someone between משה and רבי who had both תורה and greatness with no equal.

phrases.english: And was there not?!
But there was Joshua!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the praise of רבי from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that from משה until רבי, תורה and greatness were never in one person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יהושע was both national leader and a great תורה scholar, so the claim seems false.

steps.title: אלעזר was יהושע's equal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אלעזר lived at the same time as יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that יהושע was not alone at the top, because אלעזר was there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is about one person being unmatched in both areas. If אלעזר matched יהושע in תורה, then יהושע was not the single leader in both.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול, son of אהרן

phrases.english: There was Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the יהושע challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a rival of equal stature.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהושע alone combined תורה and greatness.
steps.terutzMaskana: אלעזר was his equal in תורה, so יהושע was not unique.

steps.title: Then wasn't אלעזר such a person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks about אלעזר himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was אלעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer into a new challenge: maybe אלעזר is the one who had both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אלעזר was great enough to match יהושע, then after יהושע was gone, אלעזר may have stood alone at the top. That would again break the claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah and worldly greatness, the pair the claim is about

phrases.english: But there was Elazar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the previous answer into a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from step 4, now tested on אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אלעזר himself may have been unmatched in both areas.

steps.title: פנחס was אלעזר's equal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that פנחס lived alongside אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was פנחס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אלעזר had an equal too: his son פנחס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It uses the same move again. Because פנחס matched אלעזר, אלעזר was not the single top figure.

phrases.english: There was Pinchas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אלעזר challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a rival of equal stature.

steps.title: Then wasn't פנחס such a person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about פנחס.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was פנחס!
steps.whatsHappening: Once more the answer becomes the next challenge: maybe פנחס was the one who stood alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time a rival is named, the גמרא asks whether that rival was unmatched later on. Now the target is פנחס.

phrases.english: But there was Pinchas!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the previous answer into a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from step 4, now tested on פנחס.

steps.title: The זקנים were פנחס's equals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the זקנים were there alongside פנחס.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were the Elders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the זקנים were equal to פנחס, which ends the יהושע chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the answer names a group of people, not one person. Because they matched פנחס, he was not the single top figure either.

phrases.english: There were the Elders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פנחס challenge and closes this chain.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to rivals of equal stature.

steps.title: Wasn't שאול such a person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on to שאול המלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was שאול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from a later period: שאול, the first king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול was king, which is worldly greatness, and he was also a תורה figure. So he looks like a new counterexample.

phrases.english: But there was Saul!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge from a different period.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שאול seems to have combined kingship and תורה.

steps.title: שמואל was שאול's equal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל lived in שאול's time.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל matched שאול in תורה, so שאול was not alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern as before. A rival in תורה means the king did not stand alone at the top.

phrases.english: There was Samuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאול challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a rival of equal stature.

steps.title: But שמואל died first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that שמואל died while שאול still reigned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer: שמואל died during שאול's reign, so after that שאול stood alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new kind of challenge. It accepts that the rival existed, but points out that he did not last, which left a stretch of time when שאול had no equal.

phrases.english: But he passed away!
phrases.notes: The one who died is שמואל. He died while שאול was still king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer that שמואל was שאול's equal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שמואל was there.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After שמואל died, שאול was unmatched for the rest of his reign.

steps.title: The claim means all of one's years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that the praise of רבי means being unmatched for all one's years.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking of all the years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the claim in step 4 really meant: no one was unmatched for his entire time as leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being alone at the top for part of one's reign does not count. שאול had an equal during his early years, so he does not break the claim.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sharpening of the claim is the key that answers every later challenge where the rival died or was killed.

phrases.english: We are speaking of all the years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection by narrowing the claim.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the scope of the original statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being unmatched even for part of one's reign would break the claim.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone unmatched for all his years would break it.

steps.title: Wasn't דוד such a person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from דוד המלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was דוד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge: דוד, who was both king and a great תורה figure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד was famous for both kingship and תורה, so he seems to fit the description of רבי.

phrases.english: But there was David!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דוד seems to have combined kingship and תורה.

steps.title: עירא היאירי was דוד's equal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עירא היאירי matched דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was עירא היאירי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עירא היאירי matched דוד in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern: an equal in תורה means דוד was not alone.

keyTerms.meaning: A great figure in דוד's time

phrases.english: There was Ira the Jairite.
phrases.notes: He is mentioned in שמואל ב 20:26.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the דוד challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a rival of equal stature.

steps.title: But עירא died first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that עירא died during דוד's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that עירא died while דוד was still alive, which left דוד unmatched afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same objection that was raised about שמואל. Once the rival is gone, the king may have stood alone.

keyTerms.meaning: But he died! (the rival did not outlast the king)

phrases.english: But he passed away!
phrases.notes: The one who died is עירא, during דוד's lifetime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the עירא answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that עירא was there.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After עירא died, דוד was unmatched.

steps.title: We require all of one's years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats that the claim requires being unmatched for all one's years.
steps.simpleTranslation: We require all the years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as it gave for שאול: to count, a person must be unmatched for all his years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the wording is בעינן, 'we require', instead of קאמרינן, but the idea is the same. דוד had an equal for part of his reign, so he does not count.

phrases.english: We require all the years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers using the rule from step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being unmatched for part of a reign counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only being unmatched for the whole reign counts.

steps.title: Wasn't שלמה such a person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from שלמה המלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was שלמה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names שלמה, the wisest king, as a new challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה had great kingship and great wisdom, so he seems to break the claim.

phrases.english: But there was Solomon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמה seems to have combined kingship and תורה.

steps.title: שמעי בן גרא was there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמעי בן גרא lived in שלמה's time.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was שמעי בן גרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמעי בן גרא stood alongside שלמה in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because שמעי was there, שלמה did not stand alone at the top.

keyTerms.meaning: שמעי, son of גרא, a figure in שלמה's time

phrases.english: There was Shimi ben Gera.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שלמה challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a rival in תורה.

steps.title: But שלמה killed him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that שלמה killed שמעי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he killed him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that שלמה had שמעי killed, so after that שלמה stood alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of objection as before, but this time the rival was killed instead of dying naturally.

phrases.english: But he killed him!
phrases.notes: שלמה killed שמעי, as told in מלכים א פרק ב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the שמעי answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שמעי was there.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After שמעי's death, שלמה was unmatched.

steps.title: All the years again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers again that the claim means all of one's years.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking of all the years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same rule: שלמה was not unmatched for his whole reign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעי was alive at the start of שלמה's reign. So שלמה was not alone at the top for all his years.

keyTerms.meaning: We are speaking of all the years

phrases.english: We are speaking of all the years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'all the years' rule again.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later years alone would count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole reign must be unmatched.

steps.title: Wasn't חזקיה such a person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from חזקיה המלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was חזקיה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names חזקיה, a king known for spreading תורה, as a new challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה was king and a leader in תורה, so he looks like another counterexample.

phrases.english: But there was Hezekiah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חזקיה seems to have combined kingship and תורה.

steps.title: שבנא was חזקיה's equal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שבנא lived in חזקיה's time.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was שבנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שבנא matched חזקיה in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An equal in תורה means חזקיה did not stand alone.

phrases.english: There was Shevna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חזקיה challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a rival of equal stature.

steps.title: But שבנא was killed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that שבנא was killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he was killed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that שבנא was killed, which left חזקיה unmatched afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same objection pattern again: the rival did not last through the king's whole reign.

phrases.english: But he was killed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the שבנא answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שבנא was there.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After שבנא was killed, חזקיה was unmatched.

steps.title: All the years once more
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the 'all the years' answer once more.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking of all the years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers again: חזקיה was not unmatched for his whole reign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבנא matched חזקיה for part of his reign. That is enough to show חזקיה was not alone for all his years.

keyTerms.meaning: We are speaking of all the years

phrases.english: We are speaking of all the years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'all the years' rule again.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole reign must be unmatched.

steps.title: Wasn't עזרא such a person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was עזרא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names עזרא, the great sage and leader of the returning exiles, as a new challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא led the people and was the top תורה scholar of his time, so he seems to break the claim.

phrases.english: But there was Ezra!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עזרא seems to have combined leadership and תורה.

steps.title: נחמיה was עזרא's equal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that נחמיה בן חכליה lived alongside עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was נחמיה בן חכליה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that נחמיה בן חכליה was עזרא's equal, so עזרא did not stand alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same pattern answers this last challenge. A matching figure in the same generation means no single person held the top spot alone.

keyTerms.meaning: נחמיה, son of חכליה, a leader in עזרא's time

steps.whatToRemember: Every challenge is answered in one of two ways: either someone else was equal to the leader, or, if that rival died or was killed, the claim means being unmatched for all one's years. So רבי's praise still stands.

phrases.english: There was Nehemiah ben Hacaliah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the עזרא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a rival of equal stature.

steps.title: No one combined Torah and greatness from רבי to רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא adds that from רבי until רב אשי, top-level Torah and worldly greatness were not found together in one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said: I too say that from the days of רבי until רב אשי, we did not find Torah and greatness in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא adds a statement that matches the one the גמרא just finished defending. He says that after רבי, the next leader to combine Torah and greatness was רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statement praised רבי as unique for having both Torah and greatness. רב אחא בריה דרבא extends the same idea forward and says רב אשי was the next one like this. This sets up a new challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: I too say (adding a similar statement)
Torah greatness together with worldly greatness (wealth, power)
in one place, meaning in one single person

phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said:
I too say,
phrases.notes: He's adding a statement just like the earlier one, which went up until רבי's time.

phrases.english: from the days of Rebbi until Rav Ashi
we did not find Torah and greatness
in one place.
phrases.notes: Meaning both together in one single person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a matching statement right after the earlier claim about רבי was defended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From רבי until רב אשי, no one person combined top-level Torah and worldly greatness.

steps.title: Challenge from הונא בר נתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that הונא בר נתן had both Torah and greatness in רב אשי's time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there wasn't anyone? But there was הונא בר נתן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא's claim by naming a person who seems to have had both Torah and greatness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הונא בר נתן was both a Torah scholar and a wealthy, important man, then רב אשי was not unique. This looks like a direct counterexample.

phrases.english: And there wasn't anyone?
But there was Huna bar Natan!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וְהָא הֲוָה הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the statement in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only רב אשי combined Torah and greatness in his time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הונא בר נתן lived then and had both, so רב אשי was not unique.

steps.title: הונא בר נתן was below רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that הונא בר נתן was subordinate to רב אשי, so he does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: הונא בר נתן is different, because he was subordinate to רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that הונא בר נתן does not disprove the claim, because he looked up to רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim was about someone at the very top in both areas. הונא בר נתן had both, but רב אשי stood above him, so רב אשי was still the one leader with both.

keyTerms.meaning: he would bow to him, meaning he was subordinate to him

phrases.english: Huna bar Natan is different,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵיכָף הֲוָה כַּיִיף לֵיהּ לְרַב אָשֵׁי.
phrases.english: for he was subordinate to Rav Ashi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the counterexample was not at the very top.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Having both Torah and greatness is enough to break רב אשי's uniqueness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The claim is about the supreme figure. הונא בר נתן was below רב אשי, so the claim stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'תורה וגדולה במקום אחד' discussion ends here: רבי and later רב אשי were each unique as supreme leaders in both Torah and worldly greatness.

steps.title: New משנה: deals made by a deaf-mute and by young children
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a חרש can buy and sell by gestures (בן בתירא: even by lip movements), and that young children's deals count, for movable property.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A deaf-mute signals and is answered by signals. בן בתירא says: he moves his lips and is answered by lip movements, for movable property. Young children: their purchase is a purchase and their sale is a sale, for movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists more rules made so that people can do business: a חרש may trade using gestures, and young children's buying and selling counts. Both apply to מטלטלין (movable items).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says a חרש makes deals through clear hand signals. בן בתירא is more lenient and accepts even lip movements. A separate rule says the deals of פעוטות are valid. The words 'במטלטלין' limit these rules to movable property.

keyTerms.meaning: signals with gestures and is answered with gestures
communicates with lip movements and is answered with lip movements
young children (around six to ten) who understand business

steps.confusionAlert: 'קוֹפֵץ' here does not mean 'jumps.' It refers to moving the lips. בן בתירא is the more lenient view, not the stricter one.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A deaf-mute signals and is answered by signals.
And Ben Beteira says:
He uses lip movements and is answered by lip movements — with movable property.
Young children: their purchase is a valid purchase
and their sale is a valid sale — with movable property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the end of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרש can make deals in מטלטלין by gestures (בן בתירא: even lip movements), and פעוטות can buy and sell מטלטלין.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the argument is only about movable property
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the argument between the תנא קמא and בן בתירא is only about מטלטלין. For גיטין, everyone agrees that gestures are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב נחמן said: The dispute is about movable property, but regarding divorce documents, everyone agrees it must be through gestures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב נחמן, who sets the limits of the argument in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן בתירא accepts lip movements only for business deals in movable items. For a גט, even בן בתירא agrees that a חרש needs clear gestures.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Nachman said:
The dispute is about movable property,
but regarding divorce documents —
everyone agrees it must be through gestures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the argument in the משנה reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן בתירא's leniency of lip movements applies only to מטלטלין. For גיטין, all require gestures.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a גט is treated more strictly than ordinary business, even by the lenient opinion.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious from the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן needed to say this, since the משנה already says 'במטלטלין.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It's obvious! We learned 'with movable property' in the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's statement as unnecessary, because the משנה already spells it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ends בן בתירא's view with the word 'במטלטלין.' So it seems obvious that his leniency does not reach גיטין. Why would רב נחמן need to teach it?

phrases.english: It's obvious!
We learned 'with movable property' in the Mishnah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's statement in step 33 as already stated in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב נחמן's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's own word 'במטלטלין' already limits the rule, so the statement adds nothing.

steps.title: We might have read it as 'even movable property'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that without רב נחמן, we could have read 'במטלטלין' as 'even with movable property,' which would include גיטין too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said it means 'even with movable property.' He teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב נחמן's statement is needed: the משנה's wording could be misread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'במטלטלין' could be read as 'even in movable property,' meaning lip movements work for more serious matters like גיטין and also for business. רב נחמן teaches that the word is a limit: only מטלטלין.
steps.whatToRemember: בן בתירא allows a חרש to use lip movements only for buying and selling movable items. For a גט, everyone requires clear gestures.

phrases.english: You might have said it means 'even with movable property,'
phrases.notes: Meaning lip movements would work for גיטין, and for movable items too.

phrases.english: so he teaches us that it does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא ״אַף בְּמִטַּלְטְלִין״, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the need for the statement by pointing to a possible misreading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'במטלטלין' means 'even במטלטלין,' so lip movements would also work for גיטין.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'במטלטלין' is a limit. Lip movements work only for מטלטלין, not for גיטין.

steps.title: Second version: the argument also applies to divorce documents
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב נחמן says the argument between the תנא קמא and בן בתירא about movable property also applies to גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב נחמן said: Just as there is an argument about movable property, so too there is an argument about divorce documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רב נחמן's statement from step 33. In this version, he says the opposite of what he said there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, everyone agreed that a חרש needs gestures for a גט. Here, בן בתירא's view that lip movements are enough applies to a גט too, just as it does for buying and selling.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a second version of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion that argues with step 33. It is another way the same statement of רב נחמן was passed down.

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rav Nachman said:
Just as there is a dispute regarding movable property,
so too there is a dispute regarding divorce documents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב נחמן's statement from step 33, reaching the opposite result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between the תנא קמא and בן בתירא applies to גיטין as well as to movable property.

steps.title: But the משנה says movable property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this version, because the משנה limits the rule to movable property.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: 'with movable property'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version. The משנה itself says the rule is about movable property, so how can it apply to גיטין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word במטלטלין in the משנה sounds like a limit: the rule is only for movable property. That seems to leave out גיטין, which goes against this version of רב נחמן.

phrases.english: But we learned in the mishna: 'with movable property'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second version of רב נחמן from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim (second version) that the argument applies to גיטין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says במטלטלין, which sounds like it limits the rule to movable property only.

steps.title: Read it as 'even with movable property'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה should be read as 'even with movable property,' so it does not leave out גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'even with movable property.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the משנה's word as 'even' instead of 'only.' That way the משנה includes גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same reading the גמרא mentioned in step 35 as a possible mistake. In this version, that reading is accepted. The משנה is saying the rule applies even to small matters like movable property, and also to other things.
steps.whatToRemember: The two versions of רב נחמן differ on how to read במטלטלין. Version one reads it as 'only movable property,' so גיטין need gestures. Version two reads it as 'even movable property,' so the argument applies to גיטין too.

phrases.english: Say: 'even with movable property.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 37 by reading the משנה differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: במטלטלין means 'only movable property,' which would leave out גיטין.
steps.terutzMaskana: במטלטלין means 'even movable property,' so the argument applies to גיטין as well.

steps.title: From what age can young children buy and sell?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about פעוטות and asks from what age it applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Young children: their purchase is a purchase and their sale is a sale, with movable property. And from what age?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה about young children. Then it asks how old a child must be for this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says פעוטות can make deals, but it does not give an age. The גמרא wants to know where that age starts.

keyTerms.meaning: Young children (below the age of מצוות)
And up to how much? (here: from what age?)

phrases.english: Young children: their purchase is a purchase
and their sale is a sale, with movable property.
And from what age?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפָּעוֹטוֹת מִקָּחָן מִקָּח וּמִמְכָּרָן מִמְכָּר בְּמִטַּלְטְלִין וְעַד כַּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the חרש to the next part of the משנה about young children.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age at which young children's purchases and sales count.

steps.title: רב יהודה: about six or seven
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה points to his son רב יצחק to show the age: around six or seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה pointed to his son רב יצחק: about six, about seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer. רב יהודה shows the age by pointing at his own son, who was around six or seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of only saying a number, רב יהודה gives a living example. A child that age, like his son, can already make deals that count.

phrases.aramaic: מַחְוֵי רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda pointed to Rav Yitzchak, his son:
Like a child of six, like a child of seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְוֵי רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: About six or seven years old.

steps.title: רב כהנא: about seven or eight
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא gives a slightly older age: around seven or eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: about seven, about eight.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same question. רב כהנא puts the age a bit higher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This seems to disagree with רב יהודה by about a year. The גמרא will soon explain why this is not really an argument.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Like a child of seven, like a child of eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer to step 39, a bit older than step 40.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: About seven or eight years old.

steps.title: A ברייתא: about nine or ten
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives an even older age: around nine or ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: about nine, about ten.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer, from a ברייתא. It puts the age at nine or ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three different ages. This sets up the גמרא's next move, which explains how all three fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Like a child of nine, like a child of ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third answer to step 39, older than both earlier answers.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: About nine or ten years old.

steps.title: They do not disagree: it depends on each child's sharpness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the three ages are not an argument. Each child is judged by how sharp he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree; each one according to his sharpness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the three answers together. They are not really arguing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no single fixed age. A sharp child understands business earlier, and a slower child later. So six, eight or ten can each be right for a different child.
steps.whatToRemember: The age when פעוטות can buy and sell is not fixed. It ranges from about six to ten, depending on how sharp the child is.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree;
each and every one according to his sharpness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings together the three different ages from steps 40 to 42.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The age depends on each child's sharpness, so the three opinions do not really argue.

steps.title: Why do young children's deals count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule that פעוטות can buy and sell.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why חז"ל let young children make deals that count. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a child below the age of מצוות cannot make deals that count. So the גמרא wants to know why חז"ל made an exception here.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the age is settled, the גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why חז"ל let young children's deals count.

steps.title: So the child can support himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the rule exists so the child can earn a living.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Because of his livelihood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: so that a child can support himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some children may have no other way to get food except by buying and selling. If their deals did not count, they could go hungry. So חז"ל made their deals count.

keyTerms.meaning: His livelihood, enough to live on

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the power of פעוטות to make deals is a rule of חז"ל made to help the child live. The next questions in the גמרא, about price mistakes and gifts, test how far this reason reaches.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Yaakov said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because of his livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חז"ל made the deals count so the child can support himself.

steps.title: What does the word מלתחה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק and asks what the word מלתחה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he said to the one in charge of the מלתחה: Bring out clothing for all the servants of the בעל.' What is a מלתחה?
steps.whatsHappening: Since it just quoted רבי אבא בר יעקב in the name of רבי יוחנן, the גמרא brings another teaching from them on a different topic. Here it asks the question that their teaching will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not connected to the laws of the משנה. It is linked only because the same teachers said both things. The question is about a hard word in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A wardrobe or storeroom of clothing (the word being explained)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a link to פעוטות here. The only link is that the same teachers said this teaching too.

phrases.english: 'And he said to the one in charge of the meltacha:
Bring out clothing for all the worshippers of the Baal' –
What is 'meltacha'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching from the same teachers as step 45, on a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word מלתחה in the פסוק.

steps.title: Something that folds up small and stretches out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that מלתחה refers to something that can be folded small and then stretched out again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Something that is folded up and stretched out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers what מלתחה means. רבי יוחנן reads the word as made of two words: נמלל, folded, and נמתח, stretched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מלתחה is understood as a mix of 'מל' (fold up) and 'תח' (stretch). It refers to a kind of clothing that can be folded very small and then spread out big again.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Yaakov said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Something that is folded up and stretched out.
phrases.notes: He is reading מלתחה as two words joined together: מל, folded, and תח, stretched.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּבַר הַנִּמְלָל וְנִמְתָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 46.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מלתחה means something that can be folded up small and stretched out again.

steps.title: The fine linens sent to רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that בוניים בן נוניים sent רבי four fine linens that folded down to the size of a nut or a pistachio.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: בוניים בן נוניים sent רבי four fabrics: סיבני, חומס, סלסלה and מלמלא. סיבני and חומס folded down to the size of a nut and half a nut. סלסלה and מלמלא folded down to the size of a pistachio and half a pistachio.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about very thin fabrics that could be folded tiny. It gives a real example of the 'folds small, stretches out' idea from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 47 said a מלתחה is something that folds small and then stretches out again. This story shows that such cloth really existed: each fabric could be squeezed to the size of a nut or smaller, yet opened up into a full garment.

keyTerms.meaning: When [a sage] came, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said that Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיגֵּר לוֹ בּוּנְיָים בֶּן נוּנְיָים לְרַבִּי –
phrases.english: Bonyam ben Nunyam sent to Rebbi
sivni, chomes, salsela, and malmala.
phrases.notes: These are names of very fine, thin linen fabrics.

phrases.english: Sivni and chomes: like a nut and half a nut.
phrases.notes: When folded up, that is how small they got.

phrases.english: Salsela and malmala: like a pistachio and half a pistachio.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of cloth that folds small and stretches out, matching the explanation in step 47.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some linens were so fine that they folded down to the size of a nut or a pistachio.

steps.title: What does מלמלא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the name of the fabric מלמלא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is מלמלא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the meaning of one of the fabric names. This sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the four names, the גמרא picks מלמלא because its name hints at what makes it special.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of very fine linen

phrases.english: What is malmala?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word used in the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word מלמלא.

steps.title: מלמלא means folded small and stretched
steps.stepSummary: מלמלא is something that can be folded tight and then stretched out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something that is folded small and then stretched out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מלמלא is cloth that folds small and stretches out again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name comes from נמלל, meaning squeezed or rolled up small. This ties the story back to the explanation of מלתחה.

phrases.english: Something that is folded small and stretched out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 49.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מלמלא is cloth that folds small and stretches out.

steps.title: How big a price mistake can a child make?
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the rules of פעוטות, the גמרא asks how big a price mistake in their sales is allowed before the sale is affected.
steps.simpleTranslation: And their mistake, up to how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of young children buying and selling. It asks how much of a pricing mistake is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since פעוטות can buy and sell so they can earn a living, the גמרא now needs to know the limits. Does a child's wrong price cancel the deal, and at what point?

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake, here in setting the price
Young children whose sales of small items are valid

phrases.english: And their mistake, up to how much?
phrases.notes: 'Their' means the young children, the פעוטות, from earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about fabrics and goes back to the rules of פעוטות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The limit of pricing mistakes in a child's sale.

steps.title: Up to one-sixth, like an adult
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה in the name of רבי זירא says the limit is one-sixth, the same as for an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה said in the name of רבי זירא: Up to one-sixth, like an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that a child's price mistake follows the same one-sixth rule as an adult's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children get no special looser or stricter rule. Just like with an adult, a price mistake of less than one-sixth is forgiven, a mistake of exactly one-sixth is paid back while the sale stands, and a mistake of more than one-sixth cancels the sale.
steps.whatToRemember: A child's pricing mistake is judged by the same one-sixth limit as an adult's.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yona said that Rabbi Zeira said:
Up to one-sixth, like an adult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 51.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limit is one-sixth, the same as for an adult.

steps.title: Is a child's gift valid?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether a gift given by a young child counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: His gift, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a new question: we know a child can sell, but can he give a gift? This sets up the disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling was allowed so the child could earn a living. A gift brings the child nothing, so it is not clear that the same reason applies.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a question with no clear answer yet)

phrases.english: Abaye asked:
His gift, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a child's sales to a child's gifts.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a young child's gift is valid.

steps.title: רב יימר and מר בר רב אשי disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר says a child's gift does not count, and מר בר רב אשי says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said: His gift is not a gift. מר בר רב אשי said: His gift is a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to אביי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יימר holds that the permission for a child to make deals does not include giving things away. מר בר רב אשי holds that a child's gift works just like his sale.

keyTerms.meaning: His gift is not a valid gift

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said:
His gift is not a gift;
Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
His gift is a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יֵימַר אֲמַר אֵין מַתְּנָתוֹ מַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposite answers to אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יימר: not valid. מר בר רב אשי: valid.

steps.title: רב מרדכי rejects the switched version
steps.stepSummary: The opinions were switched and sent to רב מרדכי, who sent back that this is not how the event happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: They switched it and sent it to רב מרדכי. He said to them: Go say to the son of my master: Wasn't the event like this?
steps.whatsHappening: The two opinions were passed on with the names swapped. רב מרדכי pushes back and sets up the story in the next step to show the switched version is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the switched version, מר בר רב אשי says a child's gift is not valid. רב מרדכי was present when רב אשי ruled on this, and he challenges that version.

phrases.english: They switched it and sent it
phrases.notes: They swapped the names, so it arrived as if מר בר רב אשי said a child's gift is not valid.

phrases.english: before Rav Mordechai.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִילוּ אֱמַרוּ לְבַר מָר,
phrases.english: He said to them: Go say to the son of my master,
phrases.notes: 'The son of my master' is מר בר רב אשי. The 'master' is his father, רב אשי.

phrases.english: wasn't the event like this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the switched version of the dispute in step 54.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The version where מר בר רב אשי says a child's gift is not valid.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against what רב אשי, his father, actually ruled.

steps.title: רב אשי ruled that a child's gift is valid
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי recalls that רב אשי, standing with one foot on the ground and one on the step, ruled that a child's gift is valid in every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the master was standing with one foot on the ground and one foot on the step, we asked him: What about a child's gift? He told us: His gift is a gift, whether it is the gift of a שכיב מרע or of a healthy person, whether it is a large gift or a small gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי tells the event he saw: רב אשי ruled that a child's gift counts. This proves that the view 'his gift is a gift' fits מר בר רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story places רב אשי himself behind the view that a child's gift is valid, so his son surely held the same. The ruling is broad: it covers a deathbed gift and a healthy person's gift, a big gift and a small one.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, as told by רב מרדכי, a young child's gift is valid in every case: deathbed or healthy, large or small.

phrases.english: When the master was standing
one foot on the ground
and one foot on the step,
and we said to him: His gift, what is the law?
And he said to us: His gift is a gift,
whether the gift of one on his deathbed
or the gift of a healthy person,
whether a large gift
or a small gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה קָאֵי מָר חַד כַּרְעֵיהּ אַאַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the event that רב מרדכי pointed to in step 55.
steps.raayaObject: That 'a child's gift is valid' is the view of מר בר רב אשי, as his father taught.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב מרדכי's own memory of רב אשי's ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: It settles who holds which view and shows how wide the rule is: it covers every kind and size of gift.

steps.title: New list of peace rules: order of the Torah reading
steps.stepSummary: The משנה introduces rules made מפני דרכי שלום. The first is that a כהן reads from the Torah first, then a לוי, then a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the things the Sages said because of the ways of peace: a כהן reads first, after him a לוי, and after him a ישראל, because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins a list of rules the Sages made to keep peace between people. The first rule sets a fixed order for who is called to the Torah first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the perek listed rules made for the general good of society. Now it switches to a new reason: avoiding fights. With a set order (כהן, לוי, ישראל), nobody argues over who deserves the first honor.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Because of the ways of peace: to keep people from fighting
A Jewish priest, from the family of אהרן
A member of the tribe of לוי
A regular Jew who is not a כהן or לוי

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is a main source for today's practice of calling a כהן first and a לוי second to the Torah.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
These are the matters that they said
on account of the ways of peace:
A priest reads first,
and after him a Levite, and after him an Israelite –
on account of the ways of peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים אָמְרוּ מִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and topic after the discussion about a child's gift ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah reading goes in a fixed order: כהן, then לוי, then ישראל, to prevent fights.

steps.title: Second peace rule: keep the עירוב in its old house
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's second rule: the עירוב is placed in the old house where it has always been kept, to keep peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: We place the עירוב in the old house, because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule from its peace list. The עירוב that lets neighbors carry in a shared courtyard stays in the same house where it has always been.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב חצרות is food that all the neighbors share, kept in one house. If it were moved around, people might suspect or fight with each other. So the Sages said to keep it in its usual old place. The גמרא will explain this later.

keyTerms.meaning: We make an עירוב: join the courtyard homes so carrying is allowed on שבת
Shared food placed in one house so neighbors may carry in their shared courtyard on שבת
The old house: the one where the עירוב was always placed

phrases.english: A joining of courtyards is placed in an old house –
phrases.notes: "Old house" means the house where the עירוב has always been kept.

phrases.english: on account of the ways of peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second item to the משנה's list of rules made for peace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עירוב is kept in its usual old house to avoid strife.
